 SBI's domestic NIM crosses 3%, but can the bank sustain it?
 The faster growth in loans than deposits makes deposit mobilisation and funding costs important factors in sustaining margins. However, the bank's domestic credit deposit ratio declined to 73%, providing headroom to support further loan growth.

 SBI's domestic NIM rose 11 basis points sequentially to 3.11%, with the bank reiterating its FY27 guidance of 3% or above.
The bank mobilised $10.9 billion in FCNR(B) deposits and leveraged another $8.83 billion to replace high-cost wholesale deposits.
Advances grew 18.2% year on year, outpacing 12.3% deposit growth, while the domestic credit deposit ratio declined to 73%.
CASA ratio fell 92 basis points sequentially to 38.3%, making deposit mobilisation and funding costs key to sustaining margins.
State Bank of India's domestic net interest margin (NIM) rose 11 basis points sequentially to 3.11% in the September quarter, while overall NIM expanded eight basis points to 2.94%. The improvement was aided by higher yields following the deployment of surplus FCNR(B) deposits to replace high-cost liabilities. The bank has reiterated its guidance of maintaining domestic NIM at 3% or above in FY27, with improved yields, expectations of a rate hike and a healthy credit growth outlook supporting its confidence.
 SBI mobilised $10.9 billion in FCNR(B) deposits and raised another $8.83 billion through leverage against these deposits, primarily using the inflows to substitute high-cost wholesale deposits, according to a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
 Advt 
 SBI's advances grew 18.2% year on year and 3.3% sequentially in the September quarter, while deposits increased 12.3% year on year and 4.5% sequentially. The faster growth in loans than deposits makes deposit mobilisation and funding costs important factors in sustaining margins. However, the bank's domestic credit deposit ratio declined to 73%, providing headroom to support further loan growth. Its global credit deposit ratio also eased to 82.1% from 83.1% in the previous quarter, aided by FCNR(B) inflows.
 The bank has maintained its FY27 credit growth guidance at 14-15%, supported by healthy growth in the first half and expectations of stronger disbursements in the second half. Retail advances grew 14.5% year on year, while agriculture and SME advances expanded 22.6% and 22%, respectively. Corporate advances increased 16.1%. Within retail, gold loans continued to be a strong growth driver, rising 89.3% year on year.
 CASA ratio 
However, the CASA ratio declined 92 basis points sequentially to 38.3%. The bank's ability to sustain lower funding costs will therefore remain important as it pursues its loan growth target. Around 32% of its loan portfolio is linked to the external benchmark lending rate (EBLR), 27% to the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR), 17% to Treasury bill rates and 21% carries fixed rates.
 SBI reported net interest income of Rs 49,140 crore, up 14.3% year on year and 4.6% sequentially. However, other income, excluding the NSE divestment, declined 23.2% year on year to Rs 11,780 crore, partly due to treasury losses of Rs 1,280 crore against gains of Rs 4,320 crore in the previous quarter. Operating expenses rose 9.6% year on year to Rs 33,980 crore, partly reflecting front-loaded expenditure of around Rs 850 crore on IT services, vendor payments and MAP-related payments.
 Advt 
 Consequently, reported pre-provision operating profit declined 1.4% year on year to Rs 26,940 crore, although core pre-provision operating profit grew 16%. Net profit increased 14.3% year on year to Rs 23,040 crore, supported by healthy net interest income and a one-off gain of Rs 7,300 crore from the divestment of SBI Mutual Fund shares.
Asset quality remained strong, with fresh slippages declining to Rs 5,230 crore from Rs 7,050 crore in the June quarter. Gross and net non-performing asset ratios improved sequentially by eight basis points and two basis points to 1.39% and 0.36%, respectively. The provision coverage ratio remained largely stable at 74.4%, while credit costs stood at 0.22%.
 Advt 
 The bank's ability to sustain domestic NIM above 3% will depend on whether the benefit from replacing expensive wholesale deposits can be maintained alongside its targeted credit expansion. Management remains confident of maintaining the 3% threshold in FY27, supported by improving yields and its expectations of healthy credit growth.
